总体而言还是看得出有很多心血的，但是可能经验或者人力不够。 优点： 1.游戏策略性是有难度的； 2.画风和背景音乐都挺清爽的； 3.战斗系统和养成系统有点类似于王国保卫战，英雄配合小兵配合塔，各有特色，小怪种类也很多，而且作为塔防他的怪物路线还不是完全的路径形式，有点像RTS敌方单位的感觉； 缺点： 1.游戏各数值缺乏相关说明或图鉴，比如中毒会掉多少血？各个小兵和小怪具体数值？小兵升级后数值？第三张地图那个数字塔是干嘛的？ 2.游戏内部分文本有错误，比如2级兵营升3级，显示小兵数量是8+8，但是实际是8+4； 3.游戏内容还是太少； 4.兵营只能出一种小兵且全局不允许更改，尤其是大部分时候你只有2个3个兵营，这样显得所谓兵种克制非常幽默； 5.在问题4的基础上，每种小兵只有一种进阶路线，显得过于简陋； 6.小兵寻路有点问题，尤其是城门处； 7.游戏节奏和表现力稍有问题，后期和中期没太大区别，爽不起来。我前中期辛苦运营不就是为了后期爽的吗；

It's a riff on Thronefall that has some good concepts and some of the gameplay components are fun but the overall execution needs polish. I would recommend it if were just bugs or something like that but some of these are just game breaking oversights. I hire a dragon and then go to reposition it by right clicking on it the way that you can with the other units aaaand it disappears, never to be seen again. My hero has a base attack of what seems to be 25 (going off damage numbers here), and i take a perk that increases my damage by 30% so now I hit for... 25, or 26 in some cases I think I saw. I hit refresh on the perk selection window and get... The same 3 perks even though its the second perk I am picking on that map. Enemy projectiles can be infinitely outrun but a group of big troll looking guys all start swinging their hammers when I am running past at warp speed and... Somehow hits me when I am like a quarter mile away for 150 each, amounting to a bit more than half my health bar via some weird troll telekinesis I guess. Just a lot of things that don't seem to work in a logical way, or even as described. Selecting a perk that says XYZ and then not having XYZ happen gets old quick. Feels a bit early access really. If these things get fixed I'd recommend but until then its hard not to get frustrated with it

这是一款肉鸽塔防游戏，画风不算讨喜，玩法单拎出来也不算新颖，当玩家打开它的第一关时，简洁的新手指引、含量很低的塔防要素，只有一个，玩家还走不过去的刷怪点，意义不明的三项升级选项，似乎无不彰显着低完成度这四个大字，似乎只是个套了层塔防皮的固定视角肉鸽…… 然后玩家打开了第二关，上述描述完全被颠覆的第二关。 早在pvz时期，塔防的玩法就无比成熟，而这款游戏如标题所示，最后的防线，这又是什么意思呢？对嘛，我们就是辣椒嘛，就救火嘛。但因此觉得这就是一款肉鸽那就大错特错了，本作并非采用升级加技能这种设定，而是将塔防、肉鸽等要素结合在一起，综合上一回合的通关时间、建筑完整度等获得金币，再用金币升级，而这可以决策的东西可就比教程中展现出的多得多了。 首先塔防可以建设炮台、可以建向日葵，需要决策究竟该建什么，可以赋能，可以点特殊赋能技能；然后还有英雄技能、小兵种类（新版本还增加了小兵的两个指令）。在一关过后选择完技能后思考金币要点什么时，恭喜你，发现了主城是能升级的，升级后解锁了先前建筑的升级，以及更多建筑建造的点位……该思考的更多了。 可以说肉鸽与塔防结合还是比较自洽的，塔防要素本身与固定的怪物刷新也一定程度上避免了玩家脸实在太黑导致的卡关，但玩起来还是不吐不快，由于怪物数量，aoe打起来就是舒服，而第二关刚好解锁了射手英雄，局外养成看着也稍显潦草…… 嘘，别告诉别人，要是真打不过，可以一直回到主界面然后继续这一关来刷局外养成资源…… [quote]关注&加入[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45335586/]哈密瓜的游戏乐园[/url]，咱玩家最懂玩家的心思！[/quote]

《最后的防线》是一款策略塔防游戏，玩过王座陨落的玩家都应该知道，这是一款模仿王座陨落的作品，但是带有自己的创新。 游戏的玩法很简单，白天打造和升级建筑，晚上在杀怪的同时守住主城就算胜利，随着游戏的波数增加，怪物的种类和数量都会增加。每个建筑都有自己的特性，比如房屋可以升级三次；而箭塔在建造之时并没有区别，但是在升第二级时可以在三种箭塔(火箭弹、加特林和狙击)中选择一种升级，每种箭塔的攻击方式、攻速、范围和血量都不一样；还有兵营在第一次建造时就可以在5个兵种(盾兵、弓手、骑兵、枪兵、法师)里选择其中一种进行建造，升级之后会增加兵种的数量。其他建筑增加了奴隶贩子、能力商店、聚灵塔和矿工塔，比如奴隶贩子可以购买强力的士兵单位，但是只会存在一个晚上；而能力商店则可以花费金币在此购买额外的能力；聚灵塔可以吸纳敌人的灵魂，灵魂充盈时会释放减速力场；矿工塔可以生成赋能石。 游戏和王座陨落相比增加了局内能力、赋能石、天赋和图鉴。每度过一个晚上，会获得三选一的局内能力，能力各有不同，比如所有士兵共享血量的能力非常逆天、英雄或者箭塔累计杀多少怪会掉落1金币、英雄的技能附带灼烧伤害等等。而赋能石可以增强某些建筑的能力，如箭塔可以额外发射一只箭，兵营会多一个大头兵等等。天赋可以理解为局外成长，每次通关都会获得一定数量的天赋点，天赋点可以强化士兵、英雄和建筑的数值和其他能力。 对于局外成长方面我不能理解塔防游戏里面还有增强数值这一套，不强化根本打不了，难道要大家反复刷第一关和第二关强行拉长游戏时长吗？还有就是游戏的关卡和英雄太少了，希望后续能够更新多一点，顺便再调整一下数值。没玩过王座陨落的玩家或者玩腻了想体验新鲜感的玩家，可以试试这款游戏。 [quote][b]关注→[/b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32969453/][b]✨大众点评鉴赏家✨[/b][/url] [b]新游速递 | 游戏评测 | 周免资讯[/b] [b]加入→[/b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/dzdp][b]🎮大众点评交流组🎮[/b][/url] [b]心得交流 | 试玩资格 | 聊天吹水[/b][/quote]

Last Stand: Defense is a strategy-focused survival game developed by ZiiTech Games and published by ZiiTech Games in partnership with Yuettegames. Built around a blend of tower defense mechanics, base-building systems, and roguelite progression, the game places players in a hostile post-apocalyptic world where humanity fights to reclaim its place after an alien invasion devastated the planet. Rather than focusing on a single gameplay mechanic, the experience merges resource management, tactical defense planning, and incremental character upgrades into a loop that encourages careful preparation and adaptive strategy. The result is a defensive survival game where the balance between growth and protection becomes the key to lasting through increasingly dangerous waves of enemies. The setting begins long after the collapse of human civilization. According to the game’s background story, an alien species once descended upon Earth and rapidly overwhelmed humanity through sheer biological superiority. Faced with extinction, scientists initiated a desperate final plan involving experimental genetic weapons and long-term survival chambers designed to preserve the last remnants of human life. Centuries later, the player awakens in a world where civilization has fallen into ruin and alien creatures still roam freely across the land. With only fragments of technology and scattered resources remaining, the player must rebuild a fortified settlement capable of surviving in this hostile environment. While the narrative is relatively minimal, it provides enough context to establish the stakes of the player’s mission. Humanity’s survival now depends on rebuilding defensive infrastructure and gradually pushing back the alien presence that continues to threaten the world. The atmosphere emphasizes desperation and resilience, portraying the player as one of the few remaining individuals capable of organizing a meaningful resistance against the alien forces that dominate the landscape. Gameplay revolves around defending a central base from waves of hostile enemies that attack in cycles. The player begins with a small settlement and limited resources, gradually expanding their defenses by constructing buildings that support both economic development and military strength. Structures such as farms, mines, and processing facilities generate the materials necessary to sustain growth, while defensive towers and walls protect the base from approaching threats. Because resources are limited during the early stages of the game, players must carefully prioritize which structures to build and when to upgrade them. In addition to static defenses, the game introduces active units that can participate directly in combat. Soldiers and specialized fighters can be trained and deployed to reinforce defensive lines or intercept enemy forces before they reach vulnerable structures. Each unit type has its own strengths and limitations, encouraging players to create balanced formations capable of handling multiple enemy types. Some soldiers excel at holding narrow choke points, while others perform better in open areas where mobility and attack range become more important. A major element of the gameplay loop is the alternating cycle between preparation and survival. During calmer periods, players focus on expanding their settlement, gathering resources, and strengthening defenses. When the attack phase begins, waves of alien creatures approach the base from multiple directions, forcing players to rely on the structures and units they prepared earlier. These moments can become chaotic as defenses are tested by large numbers of enemies, creating intense situations where quick decision-making can determine whether the base survives the assault. The roguelite progression system adds another layer of variety to the experience. Each playthrough offers different upgrades, abilities, and bonuses that influence how the settlement develops. Some upgrades strengthen defensive towers, while others enhance the abilities of soldiers or improve the efficiency of resource production. Because these bonuses are often presented randomly, players must adapt their strategies depending on which upgrades become available during a run. This system helps ensure that no two play sessions unfold exactly the same way. Over time, players unlock additional technologies and abilities that expand their defensive capabilities. New types of buildings, stronger units, and more powerful upgrades gradually become available as the player progresses through the game. These improvements allow the settlement to evolve from a fragile outpost into a heavily fortified base capable of resisting larger and more dangerous enemy forces. The sense of progression comes from learning how to combine these systems effectively while adapting to the escalating difficulty of enemy waves. Visually, Last Stand: Defense uses a stylized 3D perspective that prioritizes readability over high-end graphical detail. Buildings, units, and enemies are designed to be easily recognizable on the battlefield, allowing players to quickly understand what is happening even during intense combat situations. The environments reflect the devastated state of the world, with ruined landscapes, alien growths, and abandoned structures appearing throughout the map. Although the graphics remain relatively simple compared to larger strategy games, the art direction effectively conveys the atmosphere of a world struggling to recover from catastrophe. The sound design complements this atmosphere with a mixture of ambient music and tense battle themes. During preparation phases, the music remains calm and subdued, reinforcing the sense of rebuilding in a quiet but dangerous world. When enemy waves begin, the soundtrack shifts to more intense compositions that emphasize the urgency of defending the base. Explosions, weapon fire, and enemy attack sounds help bring the battles to life and reinforce the tension of each defensive encounter. One of the most appealing aspects of the game is the flexibility it offers players when constructing their defensive strategy. Some players may focus heavily on building powerful towers and defensive walls, creating a fortress capable of eliminating enemies before they reach the base. Others may prefer a more active approach that relies on strong units and strategic positioning to control the battlefield. This freedom to experiment with different strategies helps keep the gameplay engaging across multiple runs. However, the game does have a few limitations that become noticeable over longer play sessions. Because the gameplay revolves around defending against repeated enemy waves, certain missions can begin to feel repetitive after extended periods of play. The roguelite elements introduce some variation, but the overall structure of preparing a base and surviving attacks remains largely consistent throughout the experience. Another minor drawback lies in the relatively limited narrative depth. While the premise of rebuilding civilization after an alien invasion is compelling, the game does not explore its world or characters in great detail. Players primarily engage with the strategic systems rather than a deeply developed storyline. Ultimately, Last Stand: Defense stands as a solid example of how indie developers can combine familiar mechanics into something engaging and replayable. Its strategic depth, flexible defense systems, and steady progression provide a satisfying experience for players who enjoy building defenses and holding the line against overwhelming enemy forces. While it may not dramatically innovate within the genre, it delivers a focused and entertaining survival strategy game that captures the tension of defending humanity’s last stronghold. Rating: 7/10
